Registration for new PhD candidates
Are you a new PhD candidate? Then register in MyPhD as soon as possible, no later than three months after the start of your program. You also need a Training and Supervision Agreement (or Opleiding- en Begeleidingsplan). You will prepare this together with your supervisor.
What documents and information do you need for your registration?
It is helpful to have the following information on hand when registering in MyPhD:
A copy of the most relevant diploma. Questions about the validity of (foreign) degrees? If so, please contact your faculty contact (pdf).
Information about the most relevant degree: MyPhD asks for name of institution, name of programme, type of degree, date of degree.
Before a registration can enter the approval process, a passport check must be carried out. Once the registration has been submitted, please contact the faculty/departmental representative (pdf) to arrange an appointment, either in person or via Teams, for this passport check.
MyPhD also asks for a working title of the dissertation. This can always be changed at a later stage.
The details of (co-)supervisor(s). Fill in the data of (co-)promoters who are not employed by Utrecht University or UMC Utrecht as completely as possible: full name, initials, title, name of institute, address of institute, e-mail. The data of the (co-)promoter(s) who work at Utrecht University can be found in a help list in MyPhD. Please check whether you choose the correct working relation.
Please note:
Faculties themselves still request specific information and documents when registering. For questions about this, contact the faculty contact (pdf) of the faculty of your first supervisor.
Missing information or signatures may affect waiver and/or admission to the doctoral program.
For more information about the Doctoral Degree Board and about MyPhD: contact the faculty contact (pdf) of the relevant faculty/department.
For more information on technical issues surrounding MyPhD, contact servicedesk@uu.nl.
What is the Training and Supervision Agreement (TSA)?
The Training and Supervision Agreement outlines rights and obligations of the PhD candidate and the objectives of the research project. In most Graduate Schools, it also outlines an individual plan of study that must be formally approved. In MyPhD, approval is recorded digitally. Some faculty have chosen to keep the Training and Supervision Agreement (TSA) separate from the MyPhD system. Check with your Graduate School about how to arrange your TSA.
What should the (co)supervisor(s) arrange?
The appointment of the supervisor(s) must take place before the professor in question has retired or received an honorable discharge.
As (co)supervisor, ensure that the PhD candidate registers in MyPhD. Once the PhD student has forwarded the digital registration for review and approval, deal with the email sent from MyPhD requesting approval as soon as possible.
See also: the Promotion Regulations Article 4 and 5.
The registration in MyPhD is fully digital and can be forwarded for review and approval by the faculty contact person, all (co-)promoters involved, the department head (if applicable), the dean and the Doctoral Degree Board at the push of a button.
What is the role of the Graduate School?
The deans have placed the responsibility for the training and supervision of PhD candidates with the Graduate Schools. The Graduate Schools are responsible for the general admission requirements for the PhD program, education and training of PhD students, supervision and quality assurance of the PhD program.
For questions about general admission procedures, training and supervision, please contact your Graduate School.
For questions about your appointment (if applicable) and formal matters regarding the completion of your PhD program, please contact the faculty contact person (pdf) of your supervisor's faculty.
Registration in MyPhD is fully digital and can be forwarded for review and approval by the PhD Office, all involved (co-)promoters, the department head, the dean and the Office of the Board of Promotions at the touch of a button.
